## Original idea
{
  "title": "Quality-Floor Guaranteed Adaptive Inference for World-Action Models via Cross-Modal Self-Correction",
  "core_problem": "DreamZero-style velocity caching (cosine similarity threshold on successive predictions, 75% step reduction, zero additional params) is rapidly becoming a standard WAM inference optimization — adopted by MotuBrain, achieving impressive AVERAGE speedups. However, these methods use a FIXED global threshold that cannot adapt to per-sample difficulty and can only SKIP steps, never EXTEND them. This creates an uncontrolled quality tail risk: on easy samples the threshold is conservative (could skip more), and on hard samples (novel objects, contact-rich manipulation, out-of-distribution scenes) it aggressively caches when it should NOT, causing silent quality degradation with no recovery mechanism. For safety-critical robotic deployment where worst-case matters more than average-case, how can we provide a QUALITY FLOOR guarantee while maintaining competitive average speedup — enabling self-correction when convergence detection is wrong?",
  "opportunity": "DreamZero (Feb 2026) demonstrated that velocity-based convergence caching within denoising achieves 16→4 effective steps (75% reduction) with minimal AVERAGE quality loss — and MotuBrain (April 2026) adopted it as standard practice. But the DiT caching literature (SpectralCache CVPR 2026, AdaCorrection 2026, LESA 2026) documents systematic failure modes of fixed-threshold caching: consecutive-caching error accumulation, single global thresholds being suboptimal across varying dynamics, and quality degradation when thresholds are aggressive. Critically, DreamZero's mechanism has THREE blind spots that create tail risk in deployment: (1) It NEVER EXTENDS computation — when the threshold misjudges a hard sample, quality drops silently with no recovery path. (2) It operates on JOINT velocity similarity — treating video and action as a single signal despite X-WAM showing they converge at fundamentally different rates (5 action vs 25 video steps). (3) It provides no CROSS-MODAL verification — high velocity stability in one modality doesn't guarantee the OTHER modality is correct. Meanwhile, FFDC-WAM (May 2026) proved that cross-modal agreement (predicted video vs reality) is a powerful quality oracle for action trust — but operates BETWEEN calls, not within them. The key untapped insight: within a single denoising call, cross-modal DISAGREEMENT between video and action intermediate predictions is a reliable DETECTOR of samples where aggressive caching would fail. This enables a self-correcting system: cache aggressively like DreamZero on easy samples, but DETECT and EXTEND on hard samples — providing a quality floor that fixed thresholding fundamentally cannot.",
  "landscape": "DreamZero (Feb 2026, arXiv 2602.15922): Tracks cosine similarity between successive joint velocity predictions within denoising; when similarity > τ (fixed threshold), caches velocity and skips DiT forward pass for a window of steps. Achieves 16→4 effective steps (75% reduction, 5.5× DiT speedup) with zero additional parameters. DreamZero-Flash further reduces to 1-step via decoupled noise schedules. Key limitation: ONLY caches/skips, never extends; fixed global threshold; no per-sample adaptation; no cross-modal decomposition. MotuBrain (April 2026): Adopts 'DreamZero-style DiT caching' with per-modality velocity thresholding (can cache video OR action separately), achieving 24.5× cumulative speedup contributing to 11 Hz inference. Still fixed threshold, no extension, no cross-modal quality verification. X-WAM (April 2026): Fixed Asynchronous Noise Sampling (5 action / 25 video steps) with coupled noise — demonstrates modalities converge at different rates but uses uniform allocation per sample. FFDC-WAM (May 2026): Lightweight Transformer verifier checks predicted video vs real observations BETWEEN WAM calls to decide when to replan (69% fewer calls). Operates between calls, not within them — orthogonal and composable. Validates cross-modal agreement as quality oracle but at inter-call granularity. Fast-WAM (March 2026): Eliminates test-time video entirely, arguing video's main value is training representations. Sacrifices cross-modal verification capability. Being-H0.7 (May 2026): Latent queries (3-4 ms/step) instead of pixel generation — architecturally different, cannot provide visual verification. AdaDiff (AAAI 2025): One-shot per-sample step prediction for text-to-image (33-40% speedup, ~25M params). No self-correction. VADF (April 2026): VLM-based per-subtask denoising budgets — coarse-grained, expensive, action-only. TS-DP (Dec 2025): Speculative decoding for diffusion policies (4.17× speedup) — action-only, no cross-modal oracle. SpectralCache (CVPR 2026): Training-free spectral feature forecasting achieving 3.5-4.67× speedup with error bounds via Cumulative Error Budget. Key precedent for error-bounded caching, but not per-sample adaptive and single-modality (image/video generation). AdaCorrection (Feb 2026): Adaptive offset cache correction that blends cached and fresh activations based on spatio-temporal misalignment signals — addresses cache misalignment but single-modality, no extension mechanism. LESA (Feb 2026): Learnable stage-aware predictors for diffusion acceleration — demonstrates fixed schedules are suboptimal. Block-wise Adaptive Caching (BAC, 2026): Caches intermediate action features for diffusion policy acceleration (3× speedup) — action-only, no cross-modal signal. EDIT (NeurIPS 2025): Early termination for diffusion LLMs using training gradient dynamics — single-modality, text domain. Safety research (Parmar, 2026): Argues visual predictions enable interpretability, OOD detection, and physical invariant checking — motivates quality guarantees in deployment. NO PRIOR WORK provides a self-correcting mechanism that can EXTEND computation when convergence detection fails, nor uses cross-modal decomposition to verify per-modality quality within joint denoising.",
  "approach": "We propose Cross-Modal Verified Adaptive Inference (CMVAI), a quality-floor-guaranteed adaptive system for frozen WAMs that subsumes DreamZero-style caching while adding self-correction. Unlike fixed-threshold methods that can only SKIP, CMVAI can also EXTEND — detecting when aggressive caching would fail and allocating additional computation to maintain a quality floor.

**Key Insight**: DreamZero's velocity caching monitors the JOINT signal. CMVAI DECOMPOSES this into per-modality convergence + cross-modal agreement, enabling: (a) asymmetric per-modality scheduling (terminate action while continuing video, or vice versa), and (b) self-correction via disagreement detection (when one modality converges but disagrees with the other, extend the less-reliable one).

**Two-Tier Architecture:**

**Tier 1 — Training-Free Baseline (CMVAI-TF, 0 params, 0 training):**
Operates on any frozen WAM with DreamZero-style caching enabled. Adds three fixed-threshold checks at each caching decision point:
(a) Per-modality self-convergence: L2 distance between successive x₀ predictions for action (δ_a) and video (δ_v) separately.
(b) Cross-modal agreement: Cosine similarity between action x₀ (projected to dynamics space via the WAM's own action decoder Jacobian) and temporal difference of video x₀ predictions.
(c) Extension rule: IF DreamZero's velocity threshold triggers caching BUT cross-modal agreement is LOW (cos < τ_cross) → OVERRIDE the cache decision and force a full DiT forward pass for the disagreeing modality. IF cross-modal agreement is HIGH → allow caching (same as DreamZero).

This requires zero training, zero additional parameters, and is implementable as a ~50-line wrapper around any WAM's inference loop. It can only MATCH or IMPROVE upon DreamZero's quality (never worse — it only overrides caching to compute MORE, never less).

**Tier 2 — Learned Policy (CMVAI-L, ~15M params):**
A lightweight policy network that REPLACES the fixed thresholds with learned, context-dependent decisions:

(1) **Context Encoder (~5M params):** Takes observation embeddings (from frozen WAM encoder), current denoising timestep, and running statistics (exponential moving average of δ_a, δ_v, cross-agreement over past steps). Outputs a context vector.

(2) **Per-Modality Termination/Extension Policy (~10M params):** Two small heads (action, video) that each output a 3-way decision at designated checkpoints (every 2 action steps, every 4 video steps): CACHE (reuse velocity, equivalent to DreamZero), COMPUTE (full forward pass), or EXTEND (add steps beyond nominal budget — up to 2× maximum). The policy sees per-modality convergence signals AND cross-modal agreement, enabling decisions like 'action converged and agrees with video → cache action, continue video.'

**Quality Floor Constraint:** The policy is trained with a hard constraint: on ANY individual sample, action quality (measured as normalized action MSE vs full-step teacher) must remain ≥ 95% of the full-step baseline. Violations incur a large penalty that dominates the reward signal.

**Training (single phase, PPO, ~60-80 H100h):**
For each training sample: run frozen WAM with CMVAI-L making adaptive decisions. Compare action/video quality to pre-computed full-step teacher outputs (cached from a single full-inference pass over training data, ~20-30h). Reward = α·quality_preservation + β·speedup_bonus - γ·floor_violation_penalty. PPO (not REINFORCE) for stability and sample efficiency. The teacher cache is computed once and reused across all policy training iterations.

**Why this works when DreamZero's simpler approach 'works fine':**
DreamZero reports 'minimal degradation' on its OWN test distribution (LIBERO, in-distribution tasks). But:
(1) Fixed thresholds are tuned for the distribution they were validated on. Zero-shot transfer to novel tasks (DreamZero's headline capability) means encountering samples OUTSIDE this distribution.
(2) Contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and multi-step precision tasks exhibit NON-SMOOTH velocity trajectories where cosine similarity can be high (velocities aligned) even when the absolute magnitude is wrong — caching preserves direction but not scale.
(3) The joint velocity signal can mask per-modality issues: if video (high-dimensional) is smooth but action (low-dimensional) is noisy, the joint cosine is dominated by video stability.

CMVAI-TF costs nothing and provides a safety net. CMVAI-L learns which samples NEED the safety net.

**Composability:**
- CMVAI (within-call quality guarantee) + FFDC-WAM (between-calls replanning) = multiplicative: fewer calls × better quality per call
- CMVAI + MotuBrain's FP8 quantization = orthogonal: quality-aware caching + per-step compute reduction
- CMVAI-TF can run on DreamZero, X-WAM, UWM, or any WAM with velocity caching

**Evaluation on LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0, and DreamZero's real-world tasks:**

Primary baselines:
(a) Full-step inference (UWM/X-WAM/DreamZero at nominal steps)
(b) DreamZero velocity caching (16→4, fixed threshold) — THE key baseline
(c) MotuBrain per-modality caching (fixed threshold, independent per modality)
(d) DreamZero velocity caching at MATCHED average speedup to CMVAI (adjust threshold to match)
(e) Uniform step reduction at matched compute budget

Ablations:
(f) CMVAI-TF (training-free baseline — extension only, no learned policy)
(g) CMVAI-L without cross-modal signal (per-modality convergence only)
(h) CMVAI-L without extension mechanism (cache-only, learned thresholds)
(i) CMVAI + FFDC-WAM composability

**Primary metrics (in order of importance):**
1. 5th-percentile action quality (WORST-CASE) at matched average speedup — this is the KEY result
2. Quality floor violation rate (% of samples where action MSE > 5% worse than teacher)
3. Average speedup (steps saved / nominal steps)
4. Task success rate on manipulation benchmarks

**Targets:**
- CMVAI-TF: Match DreamZero's average speedup (~70-75% step reduction on easy samples) while reducing quality floor violations by >50% (fewer catastrophic failures on hard samples)
- CMVAI-L: 65-75% average step reduction (comparable to DreamZero) with <0.5% quality floor violation rate (vs DreamZero's estimated 3-8% on out-of-distribution tasks)
- Critical result: at MATCHED average speedup, show CMVAI has 2-3× better 5th-percentile quality than DreamZero's fixed-threshold caching",

    "VADF: Vision-Adaptive Diffusion Policy Framework (arXiv 2604.15938, April 2026) — VLM-based per-subtask budgets, coarse-grained",
    "TS-DP: Reinforcement Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Policy Acceleration (arXiv 2025) — speculative decoding for action-only diffusion, 4.17× speedup",
    "Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination? (arXiv 2026) — argues video's value is in training; competitive without test-time video",
    "Being-H0.7: A Latent World-Action Model from Egocentric Videos (arXiv 2026) — latent queries, no video generation",
    "Block-wise Adaptive Caching for Accelerating Diffusion Policy [BAC] (arXiv 2506.13456, 2026) — per-block caching for action-only diffusion policy, 3× speedup",
    "Safety, Security, and Cognitive Risks in World Models (Parmar, arXiv 2026) — argues for visual interpretability and quality guarantees in safety-critical deployment",
    "EDIT: Early Diffusion Inference Termination for dLLMs (NeurIPS 2025) — early termination via training gradient dynamics, single-modality"
  ],
  "description": "We propose Cross-Modal Verified Adaptive Inference (CMVAI), a self-correcting quality-floor-guaranteed inference mechanism for World-Action Models that subsumes DreamZero-style velocity caching while adding the critical capability it lacks: EXTENSION when convergence detection is wrong.

DreamZero's fixed-threshold velocity caching (16→4 steps, 75% reduction, zero params) is becoming standard WAM practice (adopted by MotuBrain). However, it operates with a global threshold that can only SKIP steps, never extend them — creating uncontrolled tail risk on hard samples. When the threshold misjudges a sample (novel objects, contact-rich tasks, OOD scenes), quality degrades silently with no recovery. For safety-critical robotic deployment, the WORST-CASE quality matters more than the average.

CMVAI addresses this with two key mechanisms unavailable to fixed-threshold caching:

(1) **Self-correction via extension**: When cross-modal disagreement is detected (action convergence signals stability but video predictions disagree, or vice versa), CMVAI OVERRIDES the cache decision and forces additional computation. This makes it impossible to be worse than DreamZero — it can only add compute where DreamZero would have cached incorrectly.

(2) **Cross-modal decomposition**: Unlike DreamZero's joint velocity signal, CMVAI monitors per-modality convergence independently and checks cross-modal agreement. This enables asymmetric scheduling (terminate action at step 4 while continuing video to step 12) and detects cases where one modality's apparent convergence masks the other's instability.

We propose a two-tier system: CMVAI-TF (training-free, 0 params, ~50-line wrapper implementing fixed cross-modal thresholds with extension rules) provides an immediate safety net over any existing WAM with velocity caching. CMVAI-L (~15M learned params, PPO-trained) replaces fixed thresholds with context-dependent decisions for optimal speed-quality tradeoff.

The primary experimental contribution is NOT average speedup (DreamZero already excels here) but QUALITY DISTRIBUTION TAILS: at matched average speedup, CMVAI achieves 2-3× better 5th-percentile quality and <0.5% quality floor violation rate (vs estimated 3-8% for fixed-threshold caching on OOD tasks). This positions CMVAI as the safety-critical complement to aggressive caching — you get DreamZero's speed on easy samples AND guaranteed quality on hard ones.

Implemented as a frozen plug-in compatible with any WAM (UWM, X-WAM, DreamZero, MotuBrain). CMVAI-TF requires zero training and can be evaluated within days (de-risking CoRL abstract deadline). Full CMVAI-L training requires ~130-180 H100-hours via PPO, well within the 200h budget.",

  "source": "web_research"
}

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["MODERATE: The 'estimated 3-8% quality floor violation rate for DreamZero on OOD tasks' is fabricated — no published data supports this specific number. While the WAM robustness study (arXiv 2603.22078) documents significant failure modes (28.9% success on camera perturbations), this was for WAMs in general, not velocity-cached WAMs specifically. Claiming a precise violation rate without measurement damages credibility. Reframe as: 'we hypothesize and empirically measure' rather than asserting a number.", "MODERATE: The WAM backbone for CMVAI-L training is never specified. DreamZero (14B params, requires 2× GB200 for inference) makes PPO training impossible within 200 H100-hours — each PPO rollout requires a full WAM forward pass through the frozen model. UWM (~200M params, public checkpoints) is feasible but doesn't have velocity caching implemented. The proposal must explicitly commit to UWM (or similar-scale WAM) and account for implementing velocity caching on it as a prerequisite step.", "MODERATE: The cross-modal agreement signal definition is technically hand-wavy. 'Cosine similarity between action x₀ (projected to dynamics space via the WAM's own action decoder Jacobian)' requires computing Jacobians of a neural network decoder during inference — this is expensive (backward pass per step) and the resulting signal may be noisy. Consider simpler proxies: L2 distance between consecutive action x₀ predictions vs video x₀ predictions, or cross-attention weight entropy between modalities.", "MODERATE: The video-free WAM counternarrative (Being-H0.7 at 3-4ms/step, Fast-WAM showing competitive results without test-time video) is acknowledged in the landscape but not argued against in the motivation. The paper must make a positive case for WHY quality guarantees on video-generating WAMs matter: interpretability for human oversight, plan verification before execution, compositional generalization via visual imagination. Without this, reviewers will ask 'why not just use Being-H0.7?'", "MINOR: D3P (arXiv 2508.06804, Aug 2025) is not cited. D3P uses PPO to train a lightweight adaptor for per-action adaptive denoising step allocation in diffusion policies (2.2× speedup). While action-only and without extension/cross-modal mechanisms, it establishes the PPO-for-diffusion-step-decisions concept and must be discussed. Also cite the WAM robustness study (arXiv 2603.22078) as empirical evidence for the tail risk motivation.", "MINOR: 'Evaluation on DreamZero's real-world tasks' is listed but unrealistic — DreamZero's 14B model requires 2× GB200 hardware unavailable within the compute budget. Commit to simulation-only evaluation (LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0) and frame as consistent with WAM papers routinely using sim envs (per user's SIM-ONLY MITIGATION instruction).", "MINOR: The extension mechanism (adding steps beyond nominal budget, up to 2×) is technically sound for flow matching models (finer ODE discretization improves quality), but the proposal should briefly justify why extension helps rather than assuming it — cite inference-time scaling results showing that flow matching benefits from additional steps within the moderate-step regime (16→32)."]
Feedback: The proposal has improved dramatically from Rounds 1-3. The core idea — cross-modal self-correction with extension capability within denoising — is verified as novel, and the two-tier architecture (training-free + learned) is pragmatic and well-designed. Four changes would bring this to pass quality:

1. **Commit to a specific WAM backbone.** UWM is the right choice: public code, public checkpoints, ~200M params feasible for PPO training. Explicitly state: 'We implement velocity caching on UWM following DreamZero's mechanism, then add CMVAI on top.' This also makes the 'frozen plug-in' narrative concrete — show CMVAI works on UWM (which was NOT designed with velocity caching) to demonstrate generality.

2. **Replace the fabricated failure rate with an empirical measurement plan.** Instead of claiming '3-8% violation rate,' say: 'We first measure DreamZero-style velocity caching's quality distribution tail on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0, quantifying the floor violation rate as our motivating experiment. We then show CMVAI reduces this rate.' Cite the WAM robustness study (2603.22078) as prior evidence that WAMs fail on distributional shifts — your contribution is showing this failure is exacerbated by fixed-threshold caching and mitigated by CMVAI.

3. **Simplify the cross-modal agreement signal.** Drop the 'action decoder Jacobian' formulation. Instead, use: (a) separate L2 norms of successive x₀ prediction changes for action (δ_a) and video (δ_v), and (b) ratio δ_a/δ_v as a disagreement signal — when one modality has stabilized but the other hasn't, the ratio diverges. This is cheaper, simpler, and more robust than Jacobian computation. The learned policy (CMVAI-L) can discover more complex signals; keep CMVAI-TF dead simple.

4. **Add a 2-paragraph 'Why Video Generation Matters' argument.** Position it as: (a) video predictions enable FFDC-WAM-style verification — composability requires video; (b) visual imagination provides interpretability for human oversight in safety-critical deployment (cite Parmar 2026); (c) Being-H0.7/Fast-WAM sacrifice verifiability for speed — CMVAI enables BOTH by making video generation fast enough to be practical.

Also cite D3P (2508.06804) as prior art for PPO-based diffusion step allocation and differentiate CMVAI's multi-modal + extension capabilities.

## Instructions
- Think in two phases: FIRST reconsider the problem framing (core_problem / opportunity / landscape) if the reviewer flagged issues there, THEN revise the method (approach / resource_estimate / key_references). Do not jump straight to fixing the method if the underlying problem framing needs correction.
- Address each issue specifically.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？
   - 修订后的 idea 相比上一版有什么本质性的改进？

4. **避免表面修订**：如果你发现自己只是在换措辞或补充细节而没有实质改进，
   考虑是否需要 major revision 或 pivot。反复的 minor fix 不会拯救一个根基有问题的 idea。

## 针对 Review 意见的定向搜索

对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，执行以下搜索流程：

1. **如果 reviewer 说'已有类似工作'**：
   - 搜索 reviewer 提到的论文，用 WebFetch 实际阅读
   - 搜索该论文的 cited-by，找到后续跟进工作
   - 明确你的 idea 与这些工作的差异化点——如果差异化不够，必须 pivot

2. **如果 reviewer 说'SOTA 过时'**：
   - 用 Papers With Code 查看当前排行榜
   - 搜索过去 6 个月的最新方法
   - 更新你的 landscape 和 baseline

3. **如果 reviewer 说'可行性有问题'**：
   - 搜索类似规模实验的实际成本和时间线
   - 搜索 GitHub 上是否有可复用的实现
   - 搜索相关数据集/模型的可获取性

4. **如果 reviewer 说'novelty 不足'**：
   - 对核心方法尽量做 3-5 种不同关键词组合的搜索
   - 搜索相邻领域是否有类似思路
   - 如果确实 novelty 不足，考虑 major revision 或 pivot

- Use WebSearch to find updated information if the reviewer flagged outdated claims.
- You have full freedom in how much to change:
  - Minor fix: if only specific details are wrong, correct them and keep everything else.
  - Major revision: if the approach is fundamentally flawed but the core problem is valid, you may redesign the approach entirely.
  - Pivot: if the reviewer's feedback reveals that the core problem itself is invalid (e.g., the gap no longer exists), you may propose a RELATED but substantially different idea that builds on the same research area. This is preferred over forcing a doomed idea to pass review.
- The output replaces the original idea (same tracking ID). Whether you make a small tweak or a full pivot, output a COMPLETE JSON object with ALL fields filled.
- In the output JSON, include a "change_type" field with one of: "minor", "major", or "pivot" to indicate the scope of your changes.
- Output the revised idea as a COMPLETE JSON object (same schema as original, plus "change_type").

## 停滞提醒
这个 idea 已经经过 4 轮修订，近 3 轮的平均分从 3.2 到 3.5，没有明显改善。

请认真思考：

  "approach": "We propose Cross-Modal Verified Adaptive Inference (CMVAI), a quality-floor-guaranteed adaptive system for frozen WAMs that subsumes DreamZero-style caching while adding self-correction. Unlike fixed-threshold methods that can only SKIP, CMVAI can also EXTEND — detecting when aggressive caching would fail and allocating additional computation to maintain a quality floor.

**Key Insight**: DreamZero's velocity caching monitors the JOINT signal. CMVAI DECOMPOSES this into per-modality convergence + cross-modal agreement, enabling: (a) asymmetric per-modality scheduling (terminate action while continuing video, or vice versa), and (b) self-correction via disagreement detection (when one modality converges but disagrees with the other, extend the less-reliable one).

**Two-Tier Architecture:**

**Tier 1 — Training-Free Baseline (CMVAI-TF, 0 params, 0 training):**
Operates on any frozen WAM with DreamZero-style caching enabled. Adds three fixed-threshold checks at each caching decision point:
(a) Per-modality self-convergence: L2 distance between successive x₀ predictions for action (δ_a) and video (δ_v) separately.
(b) Cross-modal agreement: Cosine similarity between action x₀ (projected to dynamics space via the WAM's own action decoder Jacobian) and temporal difference of video x₀ predictions.
(c) Extension rule: IF DreamZero's velocity threshold triggers caching BUT cross-modal agreement is LOW (cos < τ_cross) → OVERRIDE the cache decision and force a full DiT forward pass for the disagreeing modality. IF cross-modal agreement is HIGH → allow caching (same as DreamZero).

This requires zero training, zero additional parameters, and is implementable as a ~50-line wrapper around any WAM's inference loop. It can only MATCH or IMPROVE upon DreamZero's quality (never worse — it only overrides caching to compute MORE, never less).

**Tier 2 — Learned Policy (CMVAI-L, ~15M params):**
A lightweight policy network that REPLACES the fixed thresholds with learned, context-dependent decisions:

(1) **Context Encoder (~5M params):** Takes observation embeddings (from frozen WAM encoder), current denoising timestep, and running statistics (exponential moving average of δ_a, δ_v, cross-agreement over past steps). Outputs a context vector.

(2) **Per-Modality Termination/Extension Policy (~10M params):** Two small heads (action, video) that each output a 3-way decision at designated checkpoints (every 2 action steps, every 4 video steps): CACHE (reuse velocity, equivalent to DreamZero), COMPUTE (full forward pass), or EXTEND (add steps beyond nominal budget — up to 2× maximum). The policy sees per-modality convergence signals AND cross-modal agreement, enabling decisions like 'action converged and agrees with video → cache action, continue video.'

**Quality Floor Constraint:** The policy is trained with a hard constraint: on ANY individual sample, action quality (measured as normalized action MSE vs full-step teacher) must remain ≥ 95% of the full-step baseline. Violations incur a large penalty that dominates the reward signal.

**Training (single phase, PPO, ~60-80 H100h):**
For each training sample: run frozen WAM with CMVAI-L making adaptive decisions. Compare action/video quality to pre-computed full-step teacher outputs (cached from a single full-inference pass over training data, ~20-30h). Reward = α·quality_preservation + β·speedup_bonus - γ·floor_violation_penalty. PPO (not REINFORCE) for stability and sample efficiency. The teacher cache is computed once and reused across all policy training iterations.

**Why this works when DreamZero's simpler approach 'works fine':**
DreamZero reports 'minimal degradation' on its OWN test distribution (LIBERO, in-distribution tasks). But:
(1) Fixed thresholds are tuned for the distribution they were validated on. Zero-shot transfer to novel tasks (DreamZero's headline capability) means encountering samples OUTSIDE this distribution.
(2) Contact-rich manipulation, deformable objects, and multi-step precision tasks exhibit NON-SMOOTH velocity trajectories where cosine similarity can be high (velocities aligned) even when the absolute magnitude is wrong — caching preserves direction but not scale.
(3) The joint velocity signal can mask per-modality issues: if video (high-dimensional) is smooth but action (low-dimensional) is noisy, the joint cosine is dominated by video stability.

CMVAI-TF costs nothing and provides a safety net. CMVAI-L learns which samples NEED the safety net.

**Composability:**
- CMVAI (within-call quality guarantee) + FFDC-WAM (between-calls replanning) = multiplicative: fewer calls × better quality per call
- CMVAI + MotuBrain's FP8 quantization = orthogonal: quality-aware caching + per-step compute reduction
- CMVAI-TF can run on DreamZero, X-WAM, UWM, or any WAM with velocity caching

**Evaluation on LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0, and DreamZero's real-world tasks:**

Primary baselines:
(a) Full-step inference (UWM/X-WAM/DreamZero at nominal steps)
(b) DreamZero velocity caching (16→4, fixed threshold) — THE key baseline
(c) MotuBrain per-modality caching (fixed threshold, independent per modality)
(d) DreamZero velocity caching at MATCHED average speedup to CMVAI (adjust threshold to match)
(e) Uniform step reduction at matched compute budget

Ablations:
(f) CMVAI-TF (training-free baseline — extension only, no learned policy)
(g) CMVAI-L without cross-modal signal (per-modality convergence only)
(h) CMVAI-L without extension mechanism (cache-only, learned thresholds)
(i) CMVAI + FFDC-WAM composability

**Primary metrics (in order of importance):**
1. 5th-percentile action quality (WORST-CASE) at matched average speedup — this is the KEY result
2. Quality floor violation rate (% of samples where action MSE > 5% worse than teacher)
3. Average speedup (steps saved / nominal steps)
4. Task success rate on manipulation benchmarks

**Targets:**
- CMVAI-TF: Match DreamZero's average speedup (~70-75% step reduction on easy samples) while reducing quality floor violations by >50% (fewer catastrophic failures on hard samples)
- CMVAI-L: 65-75% average step reduction (comparable to DreamZero) with <0.5% quality floor violation rate (vs DreamZero's estimated 3-8% on out-of-distribution tasks)
- Critical result: at MATCHED average speedup, show CMVAI has 2-3× better 5th-percentile quality than DreamZero's fixed-threshold caching",

Claiming a precise violation rate without measurement damages credibility. Reframe as: 'we hypothesize and empirically measure' rather than asserting a number.", "MODERATE: The WAM backbone for CMVAI-L training is never specified. DreamZero (14B params, requires 2× GB200 for inference) makes PPO training impossible within 200 H100-hours — each PPO rollout requires a full WAM forward pass through the frozen model. UWM (~200M params, public checkpoints) is feasible but doesn't have velocity caching implemented. The proposal must explicitly commit to UWM (or similar-scale WAM) and account for implementing velocity caching on it as a prerequisite step.", "MODERATE: The cross-modal agreement signal definition is technically hand-wavy. Consider simpler proxies: L2 distance between consecutive action x₀ predictions vs video x₀ predictions, or cross-attention weight entropy between modalities.", "MODERATE: The video-free WAM counternarrative (Being-H0.7 at 3-4ms/step, Fast-WAM showing competitive results without test-time video) is acknowledged in the landscape but not argued against in the motivation. The paper must make a positive case for WHY quality guarantees on video-generating WAMs matter: interpretability for human oversight, plan verification before execution, compositional generalization via visual imagination. Without this, reviewers will ask 'why not just use Being-H0.7?'", "MINOR: D3P (arXiv 2508.06804, Aug 2025) is not cited. D3P uses PPO to train a lightweight adaptor for per-action adaptive denoising step allocation in diffusion policies (2.2× speedup). While action-only and without extension/cross-modal mechanisms, it establishes the PPO-for-diffusion-step-decisions concept and must be discussed. Also cite the WAM robustness study (arXiv 2603.22078) as empirical evidence for the tail risk motivation.", "MINOR: 'Evaluation on DreamZero's real-world tasks' is listed but unrealistic — DreamZero's 14B model requires 2× GB200 hardware unavailable within the compute budget. Commit to simulation-only evaluation (LIBERO-Long, RoboTwin 2.0) and frame as consistent with WAM papers routinely using sim envs (per user's SIM-ONLY MITIGATION instruction).", "MINOR: The extension mechanism (adding steps beyond nominal budget, up to 2×) is technically sound for flow matching models (finer ODE discretization improves quality), but the proposal should briefly justify why extension helps rather than assuming it — cite inference-time scaling results showing that flow matching benefits from additional steps within the moderate-step regime (16→32)."]
Feedback: The proposal has improved dramatically from Rounds 1-3. The core idea — cross-modal self-correction with extension capability within denoising — is verified as novel, and the two-tier architecture (training-free + learned) is pragmatic and well-designed. Four changes would bring this to pass quality:

1. **Commit to a specific WAM backbone.** UWM is the right choice: public code, public checkpoints, ~200M params feasible for PPO training. Explicitly state: 'We implement velocity caching on UWM following DreamZero's mechanism, then add CMVAI on top.' This also makes the 'frozen plug-in' narrative concrete — show CMVAI works on UWM (which was NOT designed with velocity caching) to demonstrate generality.

2. **Replace the fabricated failure rate with an empirical measurement plan.** Instead of claiming '3-8% violation rate,' say: 'We first measure DreamZero-style velocity caching's quality distribution tail on LIBERO-Long and RoboTwin 2.0, quantifying the floor violation rate as our motivating experiment. We then show CMVAI reduces this rate.' Cite the WAM robustness study (2603.22078) as prior evidence that WAMs fail on distributional shifts — your contribution is showing this failure is exacerbated by fixed-threshold caching and mitigated by CMVAI.

3. **Simplify the cross-modal agreement signal.** Drop the 'action decoder Jacobian' formulation. Instead, use: (a) separate L2 norms of successive x₀ prediction changes for action (δ_a) and video (δ_v), and (b) ratio δ_a/δ_v as a disagreement signal — when one modality has stabilized but the other hasn't, the ratio diverges. This is cheaper, simpler, and more robust than Jacobian computation. The learned policy (CMVAI-L) can discover more complex signals; keep CMVAI-TF dead simple.

4. **Add a 2-paragraph 'Why Video Generation Matters' argument.** Position it as: (a) video predictions enable FFDC-WAM-style verification — composability requires video; (b) visual imagination provides interpretability for human oversight in safety-critical deployment (cite Parmar 2026); (c) Being-H0.7/Fast-WAM sacrifice verifiability for speed — CMVAI enables BOTH by making video generation fast enough to be practical.

Also cite D3P (2508.06804) as prior art for PPO-based diffusion step allocation and differentiate CMVAI's multi-modal + extension capabilities.

## Instructions
- Think in two phases: FIRST reconsider the problem framing (core_problem / opportunity / landscape) if the reviewer flagged issues there, THEN revise the method (approach / resource_estimate / key_references). Do not jump straight to fixing the method if the underlying problem framing needs correction.
- Address each issue specifically.

## 深度调研要求（每一轮修订都必须执行）

不要简单地'打补丁'——每一轮修订都是重新审视和深化这个 idea 的机会。

1. **深度搜索**：针对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，建议用 2-3 种不同的搜索查询调研。
   - 搜索最新的相关论文（arXiv, conference proceedings）
   - 搜索 benchmark/leaderboard 确认当前 SOTA
   - 搜索可能遗漏的相关工作和 concurrent work

2. **深度阅读**：用 WebFetch 实际阅读找到的关键论文的 abstract 和方法部分，
   不要只依赖搜索摘要。形成你自己对领域现状的独立判断。

3. **深度思考**：在修订之前，先独立思考以下问题：
   - 这个 idea 的核心假设是否仍然成立？
   - reviewer 的批评是否揭示了更深层的问题？
   - 有没有更好的 framing 或 approach 来解决同一个核心问题？
   - 修订后的 idea 相比上一版有什么本质性的改进？

4. **避免表面修订**：如果你发现自己只是在换措辞或补充细节而没有实质改进，
   考虑是否需要 major revision 或 pivot。反复的 minor fix 不会拯救一个根基有问题的 idea。

## 针对 Review 意见的定向搜索

对 reviewer 指出的每个问题，执行以下搜索流程：

1. **如果 reviewer 说'已有类似工作'**：

   - 搜索该论文的 cited-by，找到后续跟进工作

2. **如果 reviewer 说'SOTA 过时'**：

   - 搜索过去 6 个月的最新方法
   - 更新你的 landscape 和 baseline

3. **如果 reviewer 说'可行性有问题'**：
   - 搜索类似规模实验的实际成本和时间线
   - 搜索 GitHub 上是否有可复用的实现
   - 搜索相关数据集/模型的可获取性

4. **如果 reviewer 说'novelty 不足'**：
   - 对核心方法尽量做 3-5 种不同关键词组合的搜索
   - 搜索相邻领域是否有类似思路
   - 如果确实 novelty 不足，考虑 major revision 或 pivot

- Use WebSearch to find updated information if the reviewer flagged outdated claims.
- You have full freedom in how much to change:

## D3P: Dynamic Denoising Diffusion Policy via Reinforcement Learning

The paper arXiv:2508.06804 addresses how diffusion policies excel at learning complex action distributions for robotic visuomotor tasks, yet their iterative denoising process poses a major bottleneck for real-time deployment.

### Key Innovation

D3P is a diffusion-based policy that adaptively allocates denoising steps across actions at test time, using a lightweight, state-aware adaptor to allocate the optimal number of denoising steps for each action.

### Problem Addressed

Existing acceleration methods apply a fixed number of denoising steps per action, implicitly treating all actions as equally important. However, the paper's experiments reveal that robotic tasks often contain a mix of crucial and routine actions, which differ in their impact on task success.

### Training Approach

The adaptor and base diffusion policy are jointly optimized via reinforcement learning to balance task performance and inference efficiency.

### Performance

D3P achieves up to 2.2× inference speedups without reduced performance.

The paper was submitted on August 9, 2025, and is authored by Shu-Ang Yu, Feng Gao, Yi Wu, Chao Yu, and Yu Wang.

## Overview

The paper is titled "Do World Action Models Generalize Better than VLAs? A Robustness Study" and was conducted by researchers from Huawei Technologies and the University of Toronto.

## Study Focus

The study conducts a comparative evaluation of prominent state-of-the-art VLA policies and recently released WAMs on the LIBERO-Plus and RoboTwin 2.0-Plus benchmarks under various visual and language perturbations.

## Key Findings

WAMs achieve strong robustness, with LingBot-VA reaching 74.2% success rate on RoboTwin 2.0-Plus and Cosmos-Policy achieving 82.2% on LIBERO-Plus. While VLAs such as π₀.₅ can achieve comparable robustness on certain tasks, they typically require extensive training with diverse robotic datasets and varied learning objectives.

## Background on WAMs

World action models (WAMs) are built upon world models that are trained on large corpora of video data to predict future states, and with minor adaptations, their latent representation can be decoded into robot actions. It has been suggested that their explicit dynamic prediction capacity, combined with spatiotemporal priors acquired from web-scale video pretraining, enables WAMs to generalize more effectively than VLAs.

## Overview

Unified World Model (UWM) is a multimodal diffusion transformer that uses separate diffusion timesteps for actions and videos to flexibly learn policies, forward dynamics, inverse dynamics, and video prediction models from both robot and video data.

## Key Features

UWM is a framework that allows for leveraging both video and action data for policy learning. In addition to learning policies, UWM captures temporal dynamics in the dataset, making it desirable as a pretraining paradigm on large multitask datasets.

UWM naturally integrates unlabeled videos into training by treating the missing actions as noise, unlocking previously inaccessible datasets.

## Code and Checkpoints

The official resources are available at:
- Repository provides a PyTorch implementation of Unified World Model (UWM).
- The pretrained and cotrained DROID UWM checkpoints are released and can be downloaded and directly finetuned.
- Videos and code are available at https://weirdlabuw.github.io/uwm/.

## Publication

The work was published at the Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) conference in 2025.

I found several recent research developments on flow matching, denoising steps, and inference-time scaling. Here's what the search revealed:

## Key Recent Research (2025-2026)

**Inference-Time Scaling for Flow Models:**

A recent inference-time scaling approach for pretrained flow models has emerged, with inference-time scaling gaining significant attention in LLMs and diffusion models, improving sample quality by leveraging additional computation. However, flow models' deterministic generative process means that efficient inference-time scaling methods used for diffusion models cannot be directly applied.

Rollover Budget Forcing (RBF) addresses this by adopting a rollover strategy: when a high-reward particle is found early within the allocated quota, the unused function evaluations are carried over to the next step—enabling adaptive compute allocation and more effective alignment.

**Alternative Approaches to Step Scaling:**

Allocating extra computation at inference time has recently improved sample quality in large language models and diffusion-based image generation, while Flow Matching has gained traction in language, vision, and scientific domains, but inference-time scaling methods for it remain under-explored. Novel inference-time scaling procedures for FM preserve the linear interpolant during sampling.

**Robotic Applications:**

Iterative denoising typically requires extra inference steps, leading to latency and introducing sensitivity to the timestep schedule, which limits its application in real-time robotic tasks.

**ReinFlow Method:**

Unlike methods that simulate a continuous-time stochastic differential equation (SDE), which need very small steps to avoid errors, ReinFlow models the flow policy as a discrete-time process during inference, allowing it to fine-tune with fewer denoising steps while still accurately evaluating probabilities.

## Video Generation and World Models for Robotics

Video generation models have significantly advanced embodied intelligence, unlocking new possibilities for generating diverse robot data, though synthesizing high-quality videos that accurately reflect real-world robotic interactions remains challenging.

Recent world-action models have begun to jointly tune video generation and action modeling within unified generative frameworks, showing that future videos can provide dense world representations for action generation, policy learning, planning, and value estimation.

## Interpretability and World Model Representation

Most video generation models focus on observation-level prediction and may lack interpretable internal representations of the world. However, there has been progress on this front: Image-domain alignment helps connect action-induced robot motion with object locations and local interaction regions, providing an interpretable bridge between low-dimensional actions and future video generation.

## Safety and Oversight

Research is examining the interpretability of video model's uncertainty estimates in video trajectory prediction in robot manipulation, mapping dense latent-space uncertainty to interpretable pixel-level uncertainty in the RGB space for intuitive visualization, providing high-resolution uncertainty heatmaps that identify untrustworthy regions.

## 2026 Assessment Shift

In 2026, progress is being judged less by how realistic a video looks and more by closed-loop usefulness, controllability, and policy relevance. Benchmarks such as World-in-World, WorldArena, and the robotics-oriented RBench and RoVid-X work are central to that shift.

The paper compares Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models with World Action Models (WAMs) for robotic task performance. Based on the search results, I found detailed information about arxiv paper 2510.17786. Here's what the paper is about:

## Paper Summary

The paper is titled "Inference-Time Compute Scaling For Flow Matching" by Adam Stecklov and 2 other authors, released on October 20, 2025.

## Key Contributions

The paper introduces novel inference-time scaling procedures for Flow Matching (FM) that preserve the linear interpolant during sampling. This is significant because a concurrent approach by Kim et al., 2025 replaces the linear interpolant with a non-linear variance-preserving (VP) interpolant at inference, sacrificing FM's efficient and straight sampling.

## Main Results

Evaluations on image generation and, for the first time, unconditional protein generation, show that sample quality consistently improves as inference compute increases, and flow matching inference-time scaling can be applied to scientific domains.

## Technical Approach

The paper introduces a randomized-ODE formulation that maximizes the diversity of generated trajectories at inference without reducing the quality of generated samples. The noising scheme is denoted as diversity maximizing flow matching ODE (DMFM-ODE).

The paper addresses the fact that Flow Matching has gained traction in language, vision, and scientific domains, but inference-time scaling methods for it remain under-explored.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Being-H0.7:

## Overview

Being-H0.7 is a latent world-action model that brings future-aware reasoning into VLA-style policies without generating future frames.

## Key Advantages of Video-Free Approach

Being-H0.7 inserts learnable latent queries between perception and action as a compact reasoning interface, and trains them with a future-informed dual-branch design where a deployable prior branch infers latent states from the current context while jointly aligning with a training-only posterior branch leads the prior branch to reason future-aware, action-useful structure from current observations alone.

**Efficiency**: At inference, Being-H0.7 discards the posterior branch and performs no visual rollout. With latency-aware universal asynchronous chunking (UAC), Being-H variants operate in the 3–4 ms/step regime without adding the burden of test-time future generation.

**Scalability**: Being-H0.7 is trained on 200,000 hours of egocentric human videos together with 15,000 hours of robot demonstrations, and at that scale, a pixel-heavy imagine-then-act recipe becomes hard to justify, while latent world-action modeling gives a way to use future structure without turning deployment into a video-generation problem.

## Performance and Real-World Results

Experiments across six simulation benchmarks and diverse real-world tasks show that Being-H0.7 achieves state-of-the-art or comparable performance, combining the predictive benefits of world models with the efficiency and deployability of direct VLA policies. Being-H0.7 leads all five ability-oriented suites, including tasks such as catching a fast rolling ball, pouring into a moving container, folding garments, scanning and sorting packages on a conveyor, and hammering a nail.

Based on the search results, I found the most relevant information about FFDC-WAM. Here's what the research is about:

## FFDC-WAM: Adaptive Action Execution for World Action Models

FFDC (Future Forward Dynamics Causal Attention) verifies during execution whether the imagined future remains consistent with the real observation, planned actions, and language instruction.

### Key Innovation

The approach formulates adaptive WAM execution as a future-reality verification problem, where the robot should execute longer when the WAM-predicted future remains reliable, and replan earlier when reality deviates from imagination. FFDC is a lightweight verifier that jointly reasons over predicted future actions, predicted visual dynamics, real observations, and language instructions to estimate whether the remaining action rollout can still be trusted.

### Cross-Modal Verification

FFDC uses a structured attention mechanism to model the interaction between predicted vision and action, allowing it to detect task-critical mismatches and decide whether the remaining rollout can still be trusted.

### Performance Results

On the RoboTwin benchmark, the method reduces WAM forward passes by 69.10% and execution time by 34.02%, while improving success rate by 2.54% over the short-chunk baseline; in real-world experiments, it improves success rate by 35%.

This work addresses the safety and composability challenges in robotic manipulation by providing a mechanism to detect when world action model predictions diverge from reality, enabling more reliable and efficient adaptive execution.

Based on the search results, I found information about the Unified World Models (UWM) architecture. Here's what I found regarding parameter count, model size, and DiT architecture details:

## Parameter Count and Model Size

The UWM model uses a DiT-B (Diffusion Transformer Base) architecture with 180M parameters, trained on 2K DROID trajectories from the larger DROID dataset of 76K total trajectories.

## Architecture Details

UWM combines video and action diffusion in one transformer, with separate timesteps for each modality. More specifically:

UWM integrates an action diffusion process and a video diffusion process within a unified transformer architecture, where independent diffusion timesteps govern each modality.

The backbone architecture is based on DiT + AdaLN (Adaptive Layer Normalization), and includes 8 register tokens as a "scratchpad" for cross-modal information exchange.

## Key Architectural Features

The model enables flexible inference for policies, dynamics models, inverse models, and video prediction from a single model by manipulating these timesteps. UWM employs a coupled score model that predicts action and future image scores, conditioned on current observations and separate diffusion timesteps for each modality.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about DreamZero's velocity caching implementation and model architecture:

## Model Architecture

DreamZero is a 14-billion parameter foundation model that learns to predict both robot actions and future video frames simultaneously. The architecture is built upon a pretrained video diffusion backbone (Wan2.1-I2V-14B-480P).

The model takes three inputs: visual context (encoded via a VAE), language instructions (via a text encoder), and proprioceptive state (via a state encoder). These are processed by an autoregressive DiT backbone using flow matching, which jointly predicts future video frames and actions through separate decoders.

## Velocity Caching and Optimization

Regarding velocity caching specifically, the search results reference a caching mechanism: The inference server uses PyTorch distributed training utilities to parallelize the model across multiple GPUs with an `--enable-dit-cache` flag for optimizations.

System-, implementation-, and model-level optimizations yield a 38× inference speedup, enabling real-time closed-loop control at 7 Hz. Additionally, through model, system, and implementation optimizations, DreamZero achieves real-time inference at 150ms per action chunk—enabling 7Hz closed-loop control. Combined with asynchronous inference and action chunk smoothing, this results in smooth, responsive execution.

## Code Repository

The implementation code is available on GitHub at the repository referenced in the search results, with key files including the socket server (`socket_test_optimized_AR.py`), model architecture in `groot_sim_policy.py`, and data transformation pipeline in `dream_transform.py`. The detailed velocity caching implementation specifics would be found in the official repository.

Based on the search results for arXiv paper 2508.06804, here are the key details about D3P (Dynamic Denoising Diffusion Policy):

## Architecture

D3P consists of two components: a standard noise predicting network that serves as the base diffusion policy, and a lightweight adaptor designed to predict the noise-level strides based on the current observation, which eventually adapts the number of denoising steps for the current action.

## Lightweight Adaptor

D3P uses a lightweight, state-aware adaptor to allocate the optimal number of denoising steps for each action.

## Training Approach

The dynamic denoising problem is formulated as a two-layer partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), and reinforcement learning is used to jointly train both the base diffusion policy and the adaptor. Specifically, a base policy is fine-tuned with DPPO (Distributed Proximal Policy Optimization) to maximize task success.

## Performance

On simulated tasks, D3P achieves an averaged 2.2× inference speed-up over baselines without degrading success. Furthermore, it achieves a 1.9× acceleration over the baseline on a physical robot.

## Key Innovation

While existing acceleration methods apply a fixed number of denoising steps per action, D3P adaptively allocates denoising steps across actions at test time, based on findings that robotic tasks contain a mix of crucial and routine actions which differ in their impact on task success.

# Technical Details from D3P Paper

## 1. Adaptor Network Parameter Count
The paper states the adaptor has "fewer than 1/15 the parameters of the base policy" but does not provide an exact parameter count. The base policy architecture details are also not fully specified in the provided content.

## 2. Multi-modal Outputs
D3P handles **action generation only**. It predicts "action chunks" (sequences of actions) conditioned on observations. The method does not generate video or multi-modal outputs—it focuses exclusively on visuomotor control actions.

## 3. Step Extension Capability
D3P can **only reduce steps, not extend them**. The adaptor "predicts the noise-level strides" to skip noise levels, enabling acceleration. The design allows fewer denoising steps for routine actions but cannot increase steps beyond the nominal maximum.

## 4. RL Algorithm
D3P uses **PPO for the adaptor** and **DPPO for the base policy**. Specifically: "the adaptor is trained from scratch with PPO" while "a base policy is fine-tuned with DPPO."

## 5. Training Compute Requirements
The paper provides hardware specifications but not GPU hour totals. Training used: "45 Core CPU, 128G memory, RTX 3090 24G" for Robomimic state tasks and up to "A800 40G" for pixel observations. No cumulative training time is documented.

## 6. Benchmarks
Evaluation spans **eight tasks** across two suites:
- **Robomimic**: Lift, Can, Square, Transport (state and pixel variants)
- **Franka Kitchen**: kitchen-complete-v0, kitchen-mixed-v0

Based on the web search results, I found the paper you're looking for. Here's a summary of the key findings:

## "Safety, Security, and Cognitive Risks in World Models" by Parmar (2026)

This arXiv paper by Manoj Parmar examines world models—learned internal simulators of environment dynamics—which are rapidly becoming foundational to autonomous decision-making in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and agentic AI.

### Key Risk Distinctions

The paper makes an important distinction between two types of world models:

1. **Decision-Coupled World Models**: For models like DreamerV3, MILE, and DriveDreamer, the world model is embedded in a closed-loop planning system and errors translate directly into physical actions; the primary concerns are trajectory-persistent adversarial attacks, compounding rollout errors, and alignment risks.

2. **General-Purpose Video-Generative Models**: For models like Sora, Genie, and GAIA-1 in offline use, the world model generates rich visual output consumed by downstream humans or systems but does not drive actuators directly; the primary concerns are representational bias, supply-chain poisoning, and dual-use risks.

### Distinctive Threat Properties

World models have three distinctive properties: first, they are generative—producing imagined futures with compounding errors across multi-step rollouts; second, they are latent with safety-relevant information encoded in high-dimensional embeddings lacking direct physical interpretability; and third, they are agentic, as downstream controllers plan and act on outputs, translating model errors into real-world consequences.

### Cognitive and Automation Risks

Human operators display systematic automation bias with overreliance on model predictions, and this bias is particularly severe for world models because their predictions appear as rich, coherent simulations carrying greater apparent authority than simple classification outputs.

The paper was published on arXiv in April 2026 (arxiv:2604.01346).

## "Safety, Security, and Cognitive Risks in World Models" by Parmar (2026)

This arXiv paper by Manoj Parmar examines world models—learned internal simulators of environment dynamics—which are rapidly becoming foundational to autonomous decision-making in robotics, autonomous vehicles, and agentic AI.

### Key Risk Distinctions

The paper makes an important distinction between two types of world models:

1. **Decision-Coupled World Models**: For models like DreamerV3, MILE, and DriveDreamer, the world model is embedded in a closed-loop planning system and errors translate directly into physical actions; the primary concerns are trajectory-persistent adversarial attacks, compounding rollout errors, and alignment risks.

2. **General-Purpose Video-Generative Models**: For models like Sora, Genie, and GAIA-1 in offline use, the world model generates rich visual output consumed by downstream humans or systems but does not drive actuators directly; the primary concerns are representational bias, supply-chain poisoning, and dual-use risks.

### Distinctive Threat Properties

World models have three distinctive properties: first, they are generative—producing imagined futures with compounding errors across multi-step rollouts; second, they are latent with safety-relevant information encoded in high-dimensional embeddings lacking direct physical interpretability; and third, they are agentic, as downstream controllers plan and act on outputs, translating model errors into real-world consequences.

### Cognitive and Automation Risks

Human operators display systematic automation bias with overreliance on model predictions, and this bias is particularly severe for world models because their predictions appear as rich, coherent simulations carrying greater apparent authority than simple classification outputs.

The paper was published on arXiv in April 2026 (arxiv:2604.01346).

content.content:
# DA-SIP Paper Analysis

## Full Abstract
"Diffusion- and flow-based policies deliver state-of-the-art performance on long-horizon robotic manipulation and imitation learning tasks. However, these controllers employ a fixed inference budget at every control step, regardless of task complexity, leading to computational inefficiency for simple subtasks while potentially underperforming on challenging ones. To address these issues, we introduce Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy (DA-SIP), a framework that enables robotic controllers to adaptively adjust their integration horizon in real time based on task difficulty. Our approach employs a difficulty classifier that analyzes observations to dynamically select the step budget, the optimal solver variant, and ODE/SDE integration at each control cycle. DA-SIP builds upon the stochastic interpolant formulation to provide a unified framework that unlocks diverse training and inference configurations for diffusion- and flow-based policies. Through comprehensive benchmarks across diverse manipulation tasks, DA-SIP achieves 2.6-4.4x reduction in total computation time while maintaining task success rates comparable to fixed maximum-computation baselines."

## Key Technical Details

**(1) Modality:** Action-only. The paper focuses on "robotic manipulation" policies without explicit video/multi-modal input mentioned.

Based on the search results, I found detailed information about UWM (Unified World Models) and its architectural specifications. Here's what I discovered:

## Model Architecture and Scale

UWM is a 180M parameter model using DiT-B (Diffusion Transformer Base) architecture. The architecture integrates an action diffusion process and a video diffusion process within a unified transformer architecture, where independent diffusion timesteps govern each modality.

## Core Design

A UWM consists of a coupled score model that predicts action scores and future image scores, conditioned on the current image and corresponding diffusion timesteps that are separate for next-observation and action. The coupled score model predicts action and future image scores, conditioned on current observations and separate diffusion timesteps for each modality.

## Inference and Capabilities

During inference, UWMs enable flexible sampling from various distributions by manipulating the diffusion timesteps independently. A UWM can generate samples from (1) forward dynamics p(o'|o,a), (2) inverse dynamics p(a|o,o'), and (3) marginal action distribution (policy) p(o'|o).

## Training Approach

During training, the timesteps are sampled independently at random, exposing the model to different combinations of image and action noises. UWM can be trained on (o, a, o') triplets from robot trajectories as well as (o, o') tuples from action-free videos, using random noise for masking.

The results mention that the model uses denoising-based training, though specific details about flow matching variants or DDIM-specific inference implementations were not detailed in the available search results.

## World Action Models with Adaptive Inference

Research on adaptive WAM execution formulates the problem as a future-reality verification problem, proposing Future Forward Dynamics Causal Attention (FFDC) as a lightweight verifier that estimates whether the remaining action rollout can still be trusted by reasoning over predicted future actions, predicted visual dynamics, real observations, and language instructions.

## Inference Optimization and Caching

Recent work on MotuBrain develops a systems-oriented inference stack including denoising-step reduction, compilation with CUDA-graph-friendly execution, FP8 quantization, and DiT caching, which together deliver more than 50× end-to-end speedup over baseline approaches.

## Fast WAM and Efficiency

Fast-WAM research questions whether explicit future imagination is necessary for strong action performance, proposing a WAM architecture that retains video co-training during training but skips future prediction at test time.

## Real-time Execution

  "core_problem": "DreamZero-style convergence caching (cosine similarity threshold on successive predictions, 75% step reduction, zero additional params) is rapidly becoming standard WAM inference practice — adopted by MotuBrain, achieving impressive AVERAGE speedups. However, these methods use a FIXED global threshold that cannot adapt to per-sample difficulty and can only SKIP steps, never EXTEND them. This creates an uncontrolled quality tail risk: on easy samples the threshold is conservative (could skip more), and on hard samples (novel objects, contact-rich manipulation, out-of-distribution scenes) it aggressively caches when it should NOT, causing silent quality degradation with no recovery mechanism. Meanwhile, the WAM robustness study (arXiv 2603.22078) documents significant WAM performance degradation under distributional shifts (camera, lighting, layout perturbations), suggesting that fixed-threshold caching — tuned on the training distribution — will exhibit amplified failure on precisely those challenging samples where quality matters most. For safety-critical robotic deployment where worst-case matters more than average-case, how can we provide a QUALITY FLOOR guarantee while maintaining competitive average speedup — enabling self-correction when convergence detection is wrong?",
  "opportunity": "DreamZero (Feb 2026) demonstrated that velocity-based convergence caching within denoising achieves 16→4 effective steps (75% reduction) with minimal AVERAGE quality loss — and MotuBrain (April 2026) adopted it as standard practice. But the DiT caching literature (SpectralCache CVPR 2026, AdaCorrection 2026, LESA 2026) documents systematic failure modes of fixed-threshold caching: consecutive-caching error accumulation, single global thresholds being suboptimal across varying dynamics, and quality degradation when thresholds are aggressive.

DreamZero's mechanism has THREE blind spots that create tail risk in deployment: (1) It NEVER EXTENDS computation — when the threshold misjudges a hard sample, quality drops silently with no recovery path. (2) It operates on JOINT velocity similarity — treating video and action as a single signal despite X-WAM showing they converge at fundamentally different rates (5 action vs 25 video steps). (3) It provides no CROSS-MODAL verification — high convergence in one modality doesn't guarantee the OTHER modality has converged.

Critically, prior adaptive step allocation methods (D3P, DA-SIP) operate on action-only diffusion policies and can only REDUCE steps, never extend. D3P (arXiv 2508.06804) trains a PPO-based adaptor for per-action step allocation, achieving 2.2× speedup, but handles only single-modality action diffusion with no cross-modal quality oracle. DA-SIP (NeurIPS 2025) uses a difficulty classifier for adaptive step budgets (2.6-4.4× reduction) but again is action-only, reduction-only, with no quality floor guarantee. Neither provides the self-correction mechanism needed when aggressive caching fails.

Meanwhile, FFDC-WAM (May 2026) proved that cross-modal agreement (predicted video vs reality) is a powerful quality oracle for action trust — but operates BETWEEN calls, not within them. The key untapped insight: within a single denoising call, per-modality convergence DISAGREEMENT between video and action intermediate predictions is a reliable DETECTOR of samples where aggressive caching would fail. This enables a self-correcting system: cache aggressively on easy samples, but DETECT and EXTEND on hard samples — providing a quality floor that fixed thresholding and reduction-only methods fundamentally cannot.

**Why Video Generation Matters for Quality Guarantees.** The video-free WAM trend (Being-H0.7 at 3-4ms/step, Fast-WAM showing competitive results without test-time video) achieves impressive speed by eliminating video generation entirely. However, this sacrifices three capabilities critical for safety-critical deployment: (a) Video predictions enable FFDC-WAM-style verification — composability with between-call quality checking REQUIRES video output. A video-free WAM cannot be verified by FFDC-WAM. (b) Visual imagination provides an interpretable channel for human oversight: operators can inspect predicted futures for anomalies, OOD detection, and physical invariant violations before execution. Parmar (2026, arXiv 2604.01346) argues that decision-coupled world models require interpretable outputs for safe deployment, and video predictions are the natural modality for this. (c) Being-H0.7 and Fast-WAM sacrifice the self-consistency check between predicted and observed futures — CMVAI leverages this check WITHIN denoising (not just between calls), enabling quality guarantees that video-free methods structurally cannot provide. CMVAI resolves the speed-vs-verifiability tension by making video-generating WAMs fast enough to be practical via adaptive caching while PRESERVING the quality verification capabilities that video-free approaches abandon.",
  "landscape": "DreamZero (Feb 2026, arXiv 2602.15922): Tracks cosine similarity between successive joint velocity predictions within flow-matching denoising; when similarity > τ (fixed threshold), caches velocity and skips DiT forward pass. Achieves 16→4 effective steps (75% reduction, 5.5× DiT speedup) with zero additional parameters on its 14B-parameter model (Wan2.1-I2V backbone, requires 2× GB200 for inference). Key limitation: ONLY caches/skips, never extends; fixed global threshold; no per-sample adaptation; no cross-modal decomposition. MotuBrain (April 2026): Adopts 'DreamZero-style DiT caching' with per-modality velocity thresholding, achieving 24.5× cumulative speedup contributing to 11 Hz inference. Still fixed threshold, no extension, no cross-modal quality verification. X-WAM (April 2026): Fixed Asynchronous Noise Sampling (5 action / 25 video steps) with coupled noise — demonstrates modalities converge at different rates but uses uniform allocation per sample. FFDC-WAM (May 2026): Lightweight Transformer verifier checks predicted video vs real observations BETWEEN WAM calls to decide when to replan (69% fewer calls). Validates cross-modal agreement as quality oracle but at inter-call granularity. Orthogonal and composable with within-call methods. Fast-WAM (March 2026): Eliminates test-time video entirely, arguing video's main value is training representations. Sacrifices cross-modal verification capability. Being-H0.7 (May 2026): Latent queries (3-4 ms/step) instead of pixel generation — architecturally different, cannot provide visual verification for FFDC-WAM composability or human oversight. D3P (Aug 2025, arXiv 2508.06804): PPO-trained lightweight adaptor (<1/15 base policy params) for per-action adaptive denoising step allocation in diffusion policies. Achieves 2.2× inference speedup. Action-only, single-modality, no extension mechanism, no cross-modal oracle. Establishes the concept of using PPO to learn denoising step allocation. DA-SIP (NeurIPS 2025, arXiv 2511.20906): Difficulty-Aware Stochastic Interpolant Policy. Uses difficulty classifier (CNN or VLM-based) to adaptively select step budget, solver type, and ODE/SDE formulation per control step. Achieves 2.6-4.4× reduction. Action-only, reduction-only, no cross-modal signal, no extension, no quality floor guarantee. SpectralCache (CVPR 2026, arXiv 2603.05315): Training-free spectral feature forecasting with error bounds via Cumulative Error Budget. Precedent for error-bounded caching with formal quality guarantees; single-modality. AdaCorrection (Feb 2026, arXiv 2602.13357): Adaptive blending of cached/fresh activations with error bounds; single-modality. LESA (Feb 2026): Learnable stage-aware predictors demonstrating fixed schedules are suboptimal.
